Some technologies, such as STATBELT Utility, statistical software packages, and many probability
apps, allow you the option to conduct a hypothesis test without first computing the test statistic.
STATBELT and these apps will ask you to input the hypotheses and the sample data, then will compute
the test statistic and P-Value for you. This is a shortcut when compared to the first two examples. But,
if you only have access to a probability calculator, you can still complete the work by finding the test
To conduct a hypothesis test for a proportion using STATBELT Utility and summarized data, follow the
Tests → Inference for Proportions → One sample → Hypothesis test.
Under “Where is the data?” choose “Summarized data.” Type the number of successes x and the
number of trials (the sample size n).
Type the proportion p from the null hypothesis into “Hypothesized proportion p₀.”
Under “Type of test,” choose Left-tailed (<), Right-tailed (>), or Two-tailed (≠) for the alternative
Type the significance level α. The results appear as soon as you type. There is no button to click.
The output from STATBELT will include the sample proportion, the test statistic, and the P-Value. Click
“Open results in a new window” for a copy you can save.
